findingDispositions.reasoning: Process placement is an architectural decision because it fixes crash fate, TCB and dependency edges, offline asset closure, wire ownership, scratch/durable authority and the semantic-universe identity boundary. Leaving TypeScript embedded-versus-worker to implementation would create the week-one fork identified by reviewer4.

bindingDecision.topology: The Rust one-shot host directly launches the absolute bundled Node.js executable and bundled provider entry point. Within an ExecutionId there is exactly one child for each (SnapshotId, TypeScriptSemanticUniverseKey); no child or compiler state crosses universes or attempts.
bindingDecision.packagingAndIdentity: Signed typescript-runtime and typescript-provider artifacts contain closed JCS identity descriptors. The descriptors pin Node/V8/modules ABI, provider build/protocol, TypeScript compiler and stdlib identities and exact payload digests. System runtimes, version ranges and install-time package resolution are forbidden.
bindingDecision.transport: Protocol-major 1 is length/digest-framed deterministic CBOR over inherited pipes. Every envelope and all sixteen frame payloads have closed schemas, bounded arrays/bytes, exact unknown/duplicate rejection, an exact state machine, and one multi-stage Analyze transaction with per-stage attribution and terminal commitments. The host streams a sealed manifest-and-chunk VFS and never passes a live worktree root. stdout is protocol-only and stderr is bounded non-authoritative diagnostics.
bindingDecision.authority: The worker is TCB and a crash-containment boundary, not a sandbox. Scratch is per-child and ephemeral. Only the host allocates identities, validates/adopts facts, writes durable state, seals the Run, derives policy and selects termination.
bindingDecision.fate: Complete plus zero exit is the only success; clean Unavailable and deterministic BudgetExhausted map to their D9 Coverage deficiencies; missing signed assets map delivery-required; crash/hang/incomplete or invalid protocol maps provider-protocol; user cancellation retains D9 interrupted precedence.

findingDispositions.verification: delivery.v2.json DL-TS/DL-D9 structure plus DL-13; check-delivery.py mutations reject embedding, cross-universe reuse, ambient Node, lost compiler/runtime identity, live-worktree transport, wire-schema/frame/state-machine/multi-stage drift, unavailable/budget/ownership/environment/network/offline-asset loss, authoritative stderr, worker durable authority and a false sandbox claim.

findingDispositions.reasoning: C-2's general ontology correctly recognizes external-scanner as a supervised implementation effect, but the accepted v1 slice excludes scanner integrations. The exclusion therefore needs an explicit product overlay rather than a false restricted-runtime diagnosis or an implementer-local D9 code.

bindingDecision.recognition: During request-validation, inspect the frozen pre-admission PlanIntent committed as SHA-256(canonical JSON v1) under opensip.plan-intent.v1. Reject when PlanIntent.analysis.admissionDescriptor.workflow.stages[*].kind is fact-derivation and .operator is external-scanner, or when the referenced PlanIntent.analysis.admissionDescriptor.contributions[*].authority is external-scanner; providerId is required and the two surfaces must agree.
bindingDecision.identityFate: REQUEST-ID-V1 allocates and atomically reserves one canonical host-owned RequestId at first trusted ingress before parsing, so RequestId is PRESENT for this later request-validation rejection. ExecutionId, AttemptRecord, SnapshotId, PlanId, RunId and Run are ABSENT.
bindingDecision.domainAndD9: Return typed domain detail FEATURE.EXTERNAL_SCANNER_NOT_IN_V1 and reuse D9 rejectionCause extension-admission-rejected / errorCode EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED. No D9 vocabulary is added.
bindingDecision.ontology: C-2 remains broader than v1. The scope overlay does not reclassify an external scanner as a Probe or claim that ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT is its blocker.

findingDispositions.verification: delivery.v2.json DL-SCOPE/DL-D9 structure plus DL-14; check-delivery.py cross-checks live OPERABILITY REQUEST-ID-V1 and mutations reject missing/optional/late RequestId, scanner admission, contradictory aggregate admission rules, post-attempt inspection, attempt identity allocation and a scanner-private D9 code.
